what: Pre-registration of a measurement pilot: how small can the Sidorenko margin of OpenAI's H be made on explicit small kernels, by size N? Committed before any real run; the only runs before it are the desk smoke tests listed under smokeTest, which are not results.
operatorGo: the operator chose the ~$10 measurement pilot over dropping the target (2026-10-12), after the Phase 0 recommendation in corpus/targets.json row sidorenko-explicit-host
question: For the 35-vertex, 66-edge bipartite graph H of OpenAI's disproof of Sidorenko's conjecture, and a nonnegative kernel W on [N] x [N] (uniform measure, points of H sampled from the first factor and faces from the second), how small can margin(W) = log t(H,W) - 66 log p(W) be made, by N and by the kernel's distance from constant? margin < 0 would be an explicit counterexample kernel.

H.definition: the incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points; t(H,W) = E_{x in [N]^13} prod_T f(x_T), f(a,b,c) = E_y W[a,y] W[b,y] W[c,y]; p(W) = E W

source.repository: github.com/openai/math at fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb (the commit pinned in corpus/openai-math/release.json; local clone /Users/carlostoledo/Projects/openai-math, clean, read as text only)

tex.definition: Table tab:complex, columns i1 i2 i3

source.agreement: the Lean table and the tex table give the same 22 triples in the same order; instruments/sidorenko/battery.py re-reads both (as text) when the clone is present and checks both sha256 values

H.checkedFacts: 22 faces, 13 points, 66 incidences, 33 covered point pairs each in exactly two faces, connected (the preprint's Prop. prop:complex (1)); primal graph of treewidth 5 — the plan's widest pairwise contraction touches 6 point indices and keeps 5

instrument.code: instruments/sidorenko/pilot.py (search, certify, time) and instruments/sidorenko/battery.py; written here from the definitions above, no code from the claimant or any third party
instrument.floatScreen: W = sigmoid(Z) (symmetric arm: Z symmetrised), U = W / mean W, margin = log t(H,U) (scale invariance: p(U) = 1); bucket elimination along an exact-DP elimination order, per-step max rescaling with a log accumulator; torch autograd on the pod (float32, TF32 off), numpy float64 with a hand-written reverse pass on a CPU fallback; every final kernel re-read in numpy float64
instrument.exactCertify: the best kernel of each cell is rationalised to A / Q (A = rint(Q W / max W), integers 0..Q); S = sum_x prod_T F(x_T), F = sum_y A A A, is computed modulo primes small enough that every pairwise contraction stays below 2^53 in float64 (so every residue is exact), recombined by the CRT under the bound S <= N^13 prod_T (M max(A)^3) and re-checked against one extra prime; the sign is the integer comparison t < p^66 <=> S N^53 M^44 < (sum A)^66 (M = N here). On the pod the residues run in float64 on the GPU; every saved kernel is decided again on the desk with `pilot.py certify DIR` (numpy on the CPU), and a cell counts as decided only when both readings give the same S
instrument.never: a float margin decides nothing; a negative float margin with a nonnegative exact margin is recorded as a slip, never a refutation

searchSpace.armsWhy: bipartite: a general N x N kernel, the kernel notion of the preprint's theorem (two finite probability spaces); symmetric: W = W^T, the form that samples to a simple graph host
searchSpace.deltasWhy: delta = rms(U - 1) = the coefficient of variation of W. The constant kernel has margin exactly 0 (red control a), so an unconstrained minimum is the trivial 0; each cell minimises the margin at a fixed distance from constant. Near constant, a doubly-centred perturbation leaves the four-cycles (H has 33) as the first nonzero term, so margin/delta^4 is reported as the scale-free reading

deltaPenalty.form: objective = margin + lambda_t ((delta - delta0)/delta0)^2, lambda_t geometric from lambda0 to lambda1 over the restart
deltaPenalty.acceptWhy: a restart competes in its cell only if |delta/delta0 - 1| <= 0.1; the actual delta is recorded

anneal.form: Gaussian noise of scale noise0 (1 - t/(0.8 S)) added to Z after each step for the first 80% of the steps

searchSpace.initsDetail: per restart, uniformly: gauss (c + s g, s in {0.5,1,2,4}, c in {-2,0,2}), block (random 2-4 x 2-4 row/column partitions with Gaussian block values, plus 0.1 noise), lowrank (c + s u v^T / sqrt(r), r in {1,2,3})
searchSpace.seedRule: round seed = first 60 bits of sha256('arm|N|delta0|round|seed'); restarts run in batches (as many as GPU memory allows, at most 64), every restart of a round derives from that seed
searchSpace.cellOrder: by N, then arm, then delta
searchSpace.timeSlices: each cell gets (remaining budget - reserve) / (cells left); time a cell does not use passes to the cells after it

plateau.rule: a cell stops early when its best float margin improved by no more than max(abs, rel |old|) over the last 8 rounds AND is above floor; a cell whose best margin is within floor of 0 keeps searching to the end of its slice

exact.rule: every cell's best kernel is decided at Q = 1024; when its float margin is below 0.001 it is decided again at Q = 16384. Q = 1024 rather than 64 because the smoke test showed rounding to 1/64 moves the margin by up to ~30% at delta = 0.125

budget.cap: $10 of RunPod GPU time, approved by the operator 2026-10-12
budget.hourlyPrice: set at launch from the chosen GPU's price; BUDGET_HOURS = (10 - 0.3 x price) / price, the 0.3 h covering image pull, battery and start-up
budget.enforcement: pilot.py stops searching at BUDGET_HOURS (10% of it reserved for exact checks and writes); the parent session terminates the pod when the pod's billed cost reaches $10, finished or not
budget.pod: tools/runpod-sidorenko.sh on a runpod/pytorch image (CUDA, torch, numpy): fetches the pilot, battery and this file at a fixed commit, runs the battery (must exit 0, else phase FAILED and nothing is searched), then the search; serves results read-only on port 8000 with _status.json

projection.deskTimings: MacBook Air M2 (fanless), 4 threads. One forward+backward per kernel: numpy 2.4 ms (N=4), 8.6 ms (N=8), 66 ms (N=12); torch-cpu batch 4: 2.7 ms (N=8), 11.7 ms (N=12), 28 ms (N=16), 84 ms (N=20) per kernel. Exact certificate at Q = 64 (Q = 1024 needs about 1.5x the primes): numpy 0.35 s (N=8), 2.9 s (N=12), 12 s (N=16), 38 s (N=20); torch-cpu float64 4.1 s (N=16), 7.4 s (N=20); 24-29 primes
projection.flopsPerKernelStep: about 32 N^6 (forward multiply-adds x 2 x 3): 0.54 GFLOP at N=16, 6.0 at N=24, 33 at N=32, 126 at N=40
projection.gpuAssumption: 5 TFLOP/s sustained fp32 on the batched contractions and at least 1.5 ms per batched step at small N (kernel launches) — an assumption until the pod's first cells report; the slices are time-based, so a slower GPU means fewer restarts, never a larger bill
projection.coverage: at 12 GPU-hours and 90 cells (~7 min each before reallocation): N <= 12 is launch-bound (thousands of restarts per cell; most will stop on the plateau rule and pass their time on), N = 16 about 8,000 restarts per cell, N = 20 about 2,000, N = 24 about 700, N = 32 about 130 (about 3.5 GB per kernel, batch about 3 on a 24 GB card). N = 40 would cost about 13 s and 10 GB per restart and is not registered
projection.deskCertifyCost: re-deciding every saved kernel on the desk is about 90 kernels at Q = 1024; the N = 32 ones take roughly three minutes each with torch-cpu float64

killCriterion: stop at the budget cap — the pilot's deadline and the pod's billed $10, whichever comes first
per cell: the plateau rule above (stop early when the best margin has stopped moving and sits above 0.001)
stop at once and report if the battery fails on the pod, or if the pod's exact reading and the desk's disagree on any S

result.what: a table, per arm, N and delta: the best float margin, the exact margin of its rationalised kernel (sign decided by integers), margin/delta^4, restarts, rounds, seconds, stop reason, and the kernel itself (integers A and Q, saved)
result.expected: no explicit small kernel violates the inequality within this search: every exact margin positive. That outcome is stated as a measurement of this search ('no kernel with N <= 32 found by these restarts has a negative margin; the smallest exact margins by N were ...'), never as a theorem that no small host exists
result.ifNegative: any exact margin < 0 is a counterexample kernel: pilot.py writes COUNTEREXAMPLE-CANDIDATE-*.json and prints it loudly; it is claimed only after the desk's independent re-decision (pilot.py certify) agrees, the kernel's integers are published, and a second exact route (a brute-force or a different elimination order) agrees at that N
result.slip: a negative float margin with a nonnegative exact margin is recorded as a slip and counted as nothing

redControls.a: a constant kernel gives exact margin exactly 0 (N x M in {4x4, 5x3, 6x6}, and W = 1/2 with Q = 2), and float margin 0 to 1e-12
redControls.b: a malformed H is refused (a triple with a repeated point; a moved point breaking 'every covered pair lies in exactly two faces'); a wrong exponent (65) breaks the constant-kernel identity at W = 1/2; a contraction that drops a face disagrees with brute force
redControls.c: the contraction agrees exactly with brute force: H itself at N = 2 (M = 2, 3; integers), 8 faces of H at N = 3, a mixed-arity hypergraph and a path over every map of all vertices (Fractions), and K_{2,2} against tr((W W^T)^2)/(N^2 M^2)
redControls.d: the exact machinery can fail loudly: a starved CRT is refused, a corrupted residue is caught by the extra prime, and the sign path reports a negative margin when one exists (C4 against p^3 on a 2-regular 6 x 6 kernel)
redControls.battery: python3 instruments/sidorenko/battery.py — 25 checks + 7 red controls with numpy, 28 + 7 with torch (torch margin, autograd and float64 residues against numpy); about 15 s on the desk

smokeTest.status: desk only, CPU, not results — run to test the code path before registration; parameters differed (300 steps, N in {4,6,8}, deltas {0.25,0.5,1,2}, budgets of 2-3 minutes)
smokeTest.observed: every exact margin positive (a last 70-second run with this file's own parameters, N in {4,5}, 20 cells, also all positive: best exact margins 0.003-0.006 at delta 0.125, 0.036-0.046 at 0.25, 12-15 at 1, 50-60 at 2); best margins at delta 0.25 fell from about 0.047 (N=4) to 0.027-0.032 (N=6) to 0.022-0.024 (N=8); at delta 1 from about 14.6 (N=4) to 7.8 (N=8); the desk re-decision (pilot.py certify, numpy) agreed with all 15 torch-run certificates

notDoing: no sampled host graph, no F_q matrix-model construction, no D in the hundreds, no N above 32, no second budget without a new go from the operator
